rulings: CF-THE-ENGLISH-SET-CODE-IS-THE-KEY (Drew, 2026-09-06): Crown Zenith is swsh12-5, its named subset Galarian Gallery is swsh12-5gg, and `panini-zenith` is a SPORTS product that is never a Pokemon key.

THE TITLE DECIDES, and every one of these titles names Crown Zenith. Classified by the card NUMBER the slug carries rather than by the title's wording alone: `GG12/GG70` and `GG12` are the Galarian Gallery number space, `108/159` is Crown Zenith's. Two rows whose titles say only "Crown Zenith" carry GG numbers and are routed to the subset on that evidence.

A YEAR CHANGE IS IN THIS LANE'S VOCABULARY. 22 rows sit under 2021/2022 sale-year slugs; Crown Zenith is a 2023 product, so the year segment moves with the product. RELOCATE takes an arbitrary destination slug and the 2026-09-06 vintage-under-sale-year list already relocates 2015 -> 1952 the same way, so this needs no new lane shape and no rematch subclass.

489 OF THESE ARE ALSO CROSS-VERTICAL SPLIT IDENTITIES: the stored cardId names sport `baseball` (one names `gaming`) while hobbyiqCardId already says pokemon. The exact-pool reader ORs the two fields, so each of those sales was being pulled into a Panini baseball pool AND a Pokemon one. planRelocatedIdentity lands BOTH fields on the destination, which is what makes this one sale in one pool again (CF-ONE-CARD-ONE-ROW-ONE-POOL).
ONE MULTI-CARD LOT IS EXCLUDED, not routed: a single sale of three different cards has no one card identity to carry.
